The test image shows split soybean stems with white/cream pith visible and small black specks scattered on the exterior. Key observations:
- Stems split lengthwise showing internal tissue
- Pith appears white/cream (not brown)
- Many small black specks scattered on the stem exterior
- Slight blue-green tinge visible on pith in some areas

The SDS reference shows interveinal chlorosis on leaves and root/stem decay, but the key diagnostic is white pith when stems are split — which matches the test image. The test image shows:

- **White/cream pith** (key SDS diagnostic — distinguishes from Brown Stem Rot which has brown pith)
- **Blue-green tinge** on pith in areas (SDS description: "Blue-green spores of the fungus can occasionally be seen on the tap root")
- Black specks scattered on exterior stem surface
- Split stems being examined — the classic diagnostic technique for SDS

The white pith is the definitive feature here, ruling out Brown Stem Rot (brown pith) and Charcoal Rot (reddish-brown pith).
